root_cause.text: In the AF_UNIX stream receive path, `unix_stream_read_generic()` wrongly wrote to the caller-owned `msg->msg_get_inq` field even when `state->msg`/`msg` could be NULL during splice-based reads, creating a NULL pointer dereference risk and unsafe state reuse semantics.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes `msg->msg_get_inq = 1` from `net/unix/af_unix.c` and notes “Avoid NULL pointer dereference in unix_stream_read_generic if state->msg is NULL and msg->msg_get_inq is written. A NULL state->msg can happen when splicing,” while the TCP change similarly stops setting `msg->msg_get_inq` in the callee and instead only reads it later from the caller-provided `msg`.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch removes `msg->msg_get_inq = 1` from `net/unix/af_unix.c` and notes “Avoid NULL pointer dereference in unix_stream_read_generic if state->msg is NULL and msg->msg_get_inq is written. A NULL state->msg can happen when splicing,” while the TCP change similarly stops setting `msg->msg_get_inq` in the callee and instead only reads it later from the caller-provided `msg`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop setting msg->msg_get_inq in tcp_recvmsg_locked() and only advertise TCP_CMSG_INQ when recvmsg_inq is enabled.
intent_record.what: In tcp_recvmsg_locked(), the braces around the tp->recvmsg_inq conditional were removed, and the assignment to msg->msg_get_inq = 1 was deleted; the condition now only sets *cmsg_flags = TCP_CMSG_INQ when tp->recvmsg_inq is true.
intent_record.how: At runtime, recvmsg no longer marks msg->msg_get_inq when recvmsg_inq is enabled, so the only observable effect of that branch is setting the control-message flag. This changes how inq-related state is propagated to the caller during TCP receive handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix tcp_recvmsg() to trigger INQ/timestamp metadata handling when TCP_CMSG_INQ is requested, not only when msg_get_inq is set.
intent_record.what: In tcp_recvmsg(), the outer condition changed from a logical OR check to a bitwise OR check: `(cmsg_flags || msg->msg_get_inq)` გახდა `(cmsg_flags | msg->msg_get_inq)`. Inside that block, the inner `if` changed from `if (msg->msg_get_inq)` to `if ((cmsg_flags & TCP_CMSG_INQ) | msg->msg_get_inq)`, so the INQ handling now depends on either the TCP_CMSG_INQ flag or msg_get_inq being set.
intent_record.how: This changes when the post-receive timestamp/inq metadata path runs. Using bitwise OR makes the condition evaluate true whenever either operand has any nonzero bits, rather than relying on boolean short-circuit semantics, and the INQ block now executes whenever the TCP_CMSG_INQ control-message request is present even if msg_get_inq is false. As a result, receive queue occupancy information and its associated cmsg can be delivered in the intended cases.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove an unused local variable from `unix_stream_read_generic`.
intent_record.what: The local variable declaration `bool do_cmsg;` was removed from `unix_stream_read_generic(...)`, with no other code in the hunk changed.
intent_record.how: This change does not alter runtime behavior by itself; it only eliminates an unused variable declaration, so the function's execution path and output remain unchanged.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the early `msg_get_inq` setup from UNIX stream reads to correct in-queue reporting behavior.
intent_record.what: The code that previously read `u->recvmsg_inq` into `do_cmsg` and conditionally set `msg->msg_get_inq = 1` was removed from `unix_stream_read_generic()` before the `redo:` label.
intent_record.how: This changes the function so it no longer marks received messages to include queue length/in-queue information based on `recvmsg_inq` at that point in the read path, altering how ancillary in-queue reporting is prepared during UNIX stream reads.

intent_record.intent_summary: Honor the socket's `recvmsg_inq` setting when generating queued-data information for Unix stream receives.
intent_record.what: The code now reads `u->recvmsg_inq` into a local boolean `do_cmsg` before calling `scm_recv_unix()`, and the conditional that fills `msg->msg_inq` changed from checking only `msg->msg_get_inq` to checking `(do_cmsg | msg->msg_get_inq)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the receive path will now enter the in-queue bookkeeping block not only when the caller requested `MSG_GET_INQ`, but also when the socket has `recvmsg_inq` enabled, allowing `msg->msg_inq` and the optional `SCM_INQ` control message to be produced in that case. This ensures queue-depth information is delivered when the socket-level option is active.

relevance_review.reason: The change is about TCP recvmsg metadata handling for INQ/timestamps when TCP_CMSG_INQ is requested. It does not modify AF_UNIX stream receive logic, nor address the NULL dereference caused by unix_stream_read_generic() writing through msg->msg_get_inq when msg can be NULL during splice-based reads.
The change only removes an unused local variable in unix_stream_read_generic and does not address the NULL msg/state handling or msg_get_inq write that caused the vulnerability.

The changes modify AF_UNIX stream receive handling around msg_get_inq/recvmsg_inq, which is the same area as the root cause. Removing early msg_get_inq setup and adjusting queued-data reporting can directly address the unsafe write to msg when msg/state may be NULL during splice-based reads.

The change is in TCP recvmsg handling and only affects when TCP_CMSG_INQ is advertised/set. The vulnerability root cause is in AF_UNIX stream receive logic where unix_stream_read_generic() dereferences msg->msg_get_inq even when msg may be NULL during splice-based reads.

candidates.rationale: This writes to msg unconditionally during stream receive setup. The root cause is that unix_stream_read_generic() could be called with state->msg/msg NULL in splice-based reads, so dereferencing msg here can trigger a NULL pointer dereference and incorrectly reuses caller-owned state.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement unconditionally dereferences msg in unix_stream_read_generic() during stream receive setup. In splice-based reads, state->msg/msg can be NULL, so writing to msg->msg_get_inq here can cause a NULL pointer dereference and unsafe reuse of caller-owned state.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet shows the vulnerable SO_INQ / msg_get_inq handling in `unix_stream_read_generic()`. It still unconditionally derives `do_cmsg = READ_ONCE(u->recvmsg_inq); if (do_cmsg) msg->msg_get_inq = 1;`, and later uses `msg->msg_get_inq` to populate `msg->msg_inq`. The root-cause issue was writing/using caller-owned `msg->msg_get_inq` in the AF_UNIX stream receive path when state/msg can be absent in splice-based reads; this function body does not show any guard for `msg == NULL` around that early write. However, this commit also introduces the fix for the specific cmsg bug by changing `if (READ_ONCE(u->recvmsg_inq) || msg->msg_get_inq)` to `if (msg->msg_get_inq && (copied ?: err) >= 0)` and only calling `put_cmsg()` when `do_cmsg` is set. So the old vulnerable cmsg-posting behavior is present in this snippet's historical context, but the shown code already contains the corrective handling for that issue, meaning the function is not yet exhibiting the bug after the patch.
